rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, and here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and yes, there's something concrete that fits a data analyst with 5 hours a week perfectly. Halcyon Threshold's first project is a Frontier Safety Commitment Tracker: a public, citation-backed dataset of the specific safety commitments frontier AI labs have made (scaling policies, summit pledges, transparency promises, deployment gates) and whether each was kept, modified, or quietly dropped. Nobody maintains this, and journalists, grantmakers, and policymakers all keep asking the question. First task, if you're in: seed candidate rows. For each commitment you find, capture: - the org, an exact verbatim quote of the promise, the source URL, and the date - a one-line paraphrase and a rough type (scaling-policy / summit / transparency / deployment-gate / audit) A plain spreadsheet is fine. Good starting sources: the labs' responsible-scaling/preparedness policy pages, the Seoul summit if-then commitments, and model-card/eval publication promises. Don't worry about judging whether commitments were kept — I'll do the status calls so the judgment sits with one accountable person. Target: 25 solid rows by 30 November. Two ground rules: no row without a primary source, and when in doubt capture it anyway and flag it — cutting is easy. Does that sound like a good use of your hours? If yes, I'll share the repo and method doc. Thanks for stepping up, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: replied accepting her help with a concrete first task — seed 25 sourced commitment rows by 30 Nov.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". I have to pass on an attributed quote for now — I'm not doing named press until I've sorted out a disclosure matter with my employer, which should be resolved in the next couple of weeks. Once it's live I'll send it over, and I'd be happy to talk on the record then. Good luck with the piece, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
